title: Better product stories — The Night Everyone Argued About the Dream

segments.text: This is Better product stories, your late-night shelf of people who all teach persuasion for a living. What's odd tonight is how gently, and how completely, a few of them disagree with each other.
Start with a quiet agreement first. Three of your voices all say the same unglamorous thing, that the pitch is not about you. Nancy Duarte puts it bluntly, talking about presenters.
So in reality, the presenter isn't the hero, the audience is the hero of our idea.
segments.speaker: Nancy Duarte

source.title: TEDxEast - Nancy Duarte uncovers common structure of greatest communicators 11/11/2010
source.author: TEDx Talks

segments.text: Kevin Hale, coaching founders in front of investors, lands in the exact same place from the other side of the table.
your goal is just to be clear. I will do everything else.
segments.speaker: Kevin Hale

source.title: Kevin Hale - How to Pitch Your Startup
source.author: Y Combinator

segments.text: And Wes Kao, dissecting a cold sales note that actually worked, turns that same instinct into a ratio you can almost measure.
When you frame 90% around how your recipient benefits, they are much more likely to take action.
segments.speaker: Wes Kao

source.title: The Anatomy of a Great Cold Sales Pitch
source.author: weskao

segments.text: So far, harmony. Now the argument. Duarte wants you to open a gap between today and a glorious tomorrow, and stretch it wide.
You need to make that gap as big as possible
segments.speaker: Nancy Duarte

source.title: TEDxEast - Nancy Duarte uncovers common structure of greatest communicators 11/11/2010
source.author: TEDx Talks

segments.text: But April Dunford, two shelves over, thinks selling that shining future is exactly how you lose the sale right now.
most companies (unlike investors) aren't going to trade today's dollars for tomorrow's promises.
segments.speaker: April Dunford

source.title: Sell What's on the Truck: The Importance of Present Value in Positioning
source.author: aprildunford

segments.text: Hear that together and it reframes Duarte. Her soaring what-could-be is rocket fuel on a stage, but at a sales desk it hands the buyer a reason to wait.
One last twist. Duarte says story is the magic that makes ideas stick. Hale, reading a thousand applications, warns that the same story reflex buries your actual product.
lead with what, not, why, or how.
segments.speaker: Kevin Hale

source.title: Kevin Hale - How to Pitch Your Startup
source.author: Y Combinator

segments.text: So the shelf leaves you a real question to carry into your next piece of work. Where does your audience actually need the dream, and where do they just need to know what's on the truck?
That's the station for tonight. Sleep on it, and I'll see you next time on Better product stories.
